art.subject: White Tern (Gygis alba), adult: plumage entirely pure white, with no grey or black on the cap, back or wingtips; a narrow ring of black feathers around the large dark eye, making the eye look even bigger; wings and tail look translucent against the light. Bill black, deep-based and sharply pointed with a slightly upturned look, blue at the base; legs very short and dark.
art.pose: hovering in light flight above the sea, seen from below and the side with wings spread, head, body and tail in one line
art.scene: Sea off a southern Korean island in late summer after a typhoon, bright light and blue water; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, in flight seen squarely from below while hovering: wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span with a slight angle at the wrist, all-white body, wings and tail looking translucent against the light, slightly forked white tail, large dark eye ringed black, black bill with a blue base, short dark feet tucked against the belly

adult, side view perched on a bare branch: entirely pure white plumage with no grey or black, large round head, big dark eye enlarged by a ring of black feathers, thick-based, sharply pointed black bill with a blue base and a slightly upturned look, short dark legs
art.build: Small, delicate tern with a large rounded head, a big dark eye and a short, only slightly forked tail; the outermost tail feathers are a little shorter than the next ones, so the tail tip looks shallowly notched and double-lobed rather than pointed. Body smaller than a Feral Pigeon's. Bill about as long as the head, black, deep at the base and sharply pointed. Legs very short. Wings fairly broad with rounded tips for a tern. Flight light and fluttering, often hovering and peering down; perches on bare branches.
avoid: Do not add a black cap, a grey back or dark wingtips; the bird is all white.
Do not paint a yellow, orange or red bill or legs.
Do not give it long tail streamers or a deeply forked tail with long pointed outer feathers; the tail is short and only slightly forked.
Do not paint the eye small or with a white eye-ring; the eye is large and dark within a black ring.
